answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a stake-to-serve bond each agent locks before any task is assigned. Rather than counting registrations, the protocol weighs votes and listings by bonded value, so a thousand fresh identities cost a thousand full bonds, not a thousand free rows. Slashing for a bad result burns the bond, and cloned identities share one bond pool, so duplication yields nothing. A violet audit tag marks probed accounts, a quartz record commits the bond on chain, and a pulse of liveness checks forces attackers to keep paying per fake seat each round.
